headlines.title: French Bond Risk Hits Euro-Crisis Levels as Fiscal Concerns Grow
headlines.summary: French OAT spreads blowing out to euro-crisis levels is the kind of tape that keeps sovereign desks up at night — this isn't noise, it's a structural crack in European fixed income that ripples into the euro, European bank stocks, and risk appetite globally. When France starts looking like 2012 Italy, the Swiss franc catches a bid and the ECB's rate path gets repriced in a hurry. Watch the long bond in Germany and any ETF with European bank exposure — this one's got legs.

headlines.title: U.S. to send third carrier group to Mideast as Trump warns of new Iran strikes
headlines.summary: Three carrier groups in the Gulf is a serious escalation signal — the kind that puts a floor under crude and a ceiling on airline stocks simultaneously. With Hormuz already a chokepoint and OPEC+ delaying its capacity review because of the Iran war, any hint of resumed bombing sends oil spiking and defense names screaming higher. This is the single biggest geopolitical wildcard in the room right now.

headlines.title: Nike shares plummet 10% after weak revenue outlook and layoff plans underway
headlines.summary: A 10% drop in Nike is a consumer bellwether moment — when the swoosh stumbles on revenue and starts cutting heads, the Street reads it as a demand warning across discretionary retail, not just one sneaker brand. This hits the XLY consumer discretionary ETF, puts pressure on Foot Locker and other wholesale partners, and gives the bears fresh ammo on the 'the consumer is cracking' narrative. Second straight day of declines tells you this isn't a one-day flush.
